romance_success.title: Fungus Among Us
romance_success.text: Malcolm moved into the (thoroughly ventilated) bedroom. He writes you a poem every morning. They are all extremely dark and extremely about you. He has started saying 'please' in a way that makes you blush.

romance_failure.title: Spore Loser
romance_failure.text: Malcolm left to haunt a basement in Portland. He self-published a chapbook about you called 'Remediation.' Every review is just someone coughing.

friend_success.title: Mildew Friends Forever
friend_success.text: Malcolm is your best gloomy friend. He sits on your couch in head-to-toe black and critiques your TV shows. Against all odds, he is growing. Emotionally, this time.

friend_failure.title: Rot in Peace
friend_failure.text: Malcolm is gone. Sometimes a dark spot appears on the ceiling in the shape of a frowning face. You paint over it. It comes back. It always comes back.

lines: *The stain on the wall shivers. Spores drift up like dark glitter. A pale man in black unfolds himself from the plaster.*
Ugh. Light. Who let the light in.
I am Malcolm. I am the mold. I am the slow, creeping truth that every house eventually [rots|rot].

choices.text: That's so dramatic. I kind of love it.
Are you... okay?
Get off my wall.

lines: Everything rots. Your house. Your hopes. That banana you left on the counter three days ago.
I wrote a poem about it. It's called 'Banana.' It's forty pages.
...Where was I. Ah, yes. Despair.

choices.text: That's so dramatic. I kind of love it.
Are you... okay?
Get off my wall.

lines: *He blinks, slowly, like a cat that has been complimented by a lesser cat.*
Nobody has ever called me dramatic in a nice tone before.
Usually it's 'oh my god, what is that SMELL,' and then bleach. So much bleach.
Okay? No. I am a fungus. I am never okay. Okay is for drywall.
...But thank you for asking. Nobody asks. They just spray.
*He shudders. Not unhappily.*
Say that again. ...No. Don't. I'm fine. Everything is fine.
Leave me now. I must brood. The afternoon light is hitting the baseboard at a deeply upsetting angle.
I'll be here. Spreading.
You came back. Nobody comes back. What do you want? Is it suffering? I can arrange suffering.
I've written you a poem. It's about you. It's also about rot. Most of them are about rot.

choices.text: Read it to me.
Only if it's short.
Hard pass.
Lukey says you drink his leaks.

lines: *He clears his throat. A small cloud of spores escapes.*
'Ode to the Homeowner.' Ahem.
*Thou camest with thy [bleach] and thy terrible lamp. / And I, a stain, did watch thee, being damp. / Thou art a window I can never open. / Also thou hast a nice face. That is all I am hoping.*
...It needs work.

choices.text: That was beautiful.
The last line didn't rhyme.

lines: Don't. Say. That word.
*He clutches the wall. A whole patch of him goes pale.*
...Forgive me. Childhood trauma. The previous owners had a spray bottle and no sense of mercy.
*His cheeks go from grey to a slightly warmer grey.*
Stop it. Compliments make me grow. Literally. Look. I'm spreading.
*He is, in fact, spreading.*
Rhyme is a cage, {player}. Rhyme is for greeting cards and people who are happy.
...But fine. I'll rewrite it. Tonight. Alone. In the dark. Where I do my best work.
Short. Fine.
*Damp. / Dark. / You.*
It's a haiku. It's missing a line, because I am also missing something.
You: That's actually... really good.
I know. I hate that I'm good.
*He nods slowly, as if this confirms everything he has ever believed.*
Of course. Nobody wants the poem. Nobody wants the mold.
I'll just be here. Being an air quality concern.
*His eyes narrow.*
Lukey. That dripping oaf. He thinks he's so wholesome, with his flannel and his... moisture.
Yes. I drink what he spills. It's codependent. It's disgusting. It's the most stable relationship I've ever had.
If he ever gets fixed, I'll dry up. I'll become a regular wall. Beige. [Healthy|healthy].
*He says the word like it's a slur.*
Can you imagine me going on walks. Drinking water on purpose. Having hobbies that are not weeping.
Leave. Before I start enjoying this.
Actually, wait— no. Go. Go. I'll write about this later.
*Malcolm is lying on the floor beneath his stain, staring at the ceiling.*
I've figured it out. You're going to fix me, aren't you. Scrub me. Seal me. Paint me over in some cheerful [eggshell].
...Do it. Tell me what to do. I'm so tired of deciding how to be miserable.

choices.text: Then here's an order: let me take care of you.
I'm not going to boss you around, Malcolm. You get to choose.
Fine. Stop whining and get in the bucket.
Lukey's going to dry you out first. Gently.

lines: Eggshell. The color of giving up. The color of a dentist's waiting room.
*He shudders so hard a spore falls out of his hair.*
Well? Command me. Or don't. I'm not your mother. I'm your wall.

choices.text: Then here's an order: let me take care of you.
I'm not going to boss you around, Malcolm. You get to choose.
Fine. Stop whining and get in the bucket.

lines: *He goes very still.*
...Say that one more time. Slowly. I want to remember it for a poem I will never show anyone.
You: Let me take care of you.
*He reaches for your hand. His fingers are cold and slightly fuzzy.*
Fine. Yes. Take care of me. Ruin my entire aesthetic.
Choose? Me? Do you know what happens when I choose things? I chose to grow in a BEDROOM.
*He sits up. Considers. The spores drift a little slower.*
...Okay. I choose to not hate you. Today. That's a lot for me. Don't make it weird.
*His eyes go wide. Then flutter closed.*
Oh, that's— yes. That's the energy. I'm getting in the bucket.
You know this is extremely unhealthy, right? For both of us? I love it. I hate that I love it.
Lukey. Of course it's Lukey. Lukey and his big, wet heart.
*He stares at the wall that backs onto the kitchen.*
Tell him... no. Don't tell him anything. Tell him his pipes are fine. Grudgingly fine.
Next time... bring the scrub brush. And the primer.
And whatever this feeling is. I want it sealed in.
*Malcolm looks different. Paler. Drier. His stain has shrunk to the size of a dinner plate.*
The leak's gone. Lukey's fixed. I'm drying out, {player}. I feel... [light].
It's horrible. I think I might be okay. Get it over with before it gets worse.
Light. Like a feeling. Not the lamp. Never the lamp.
*Malcolm stands before his stain, holding out a scrub brush like a sword he is surrendering.*
It's time. Remediate me.
Any last words, before I become drywall?

choices.text: I love you. Even the toxic parts.
I love you. But Malcolm, you're toxic.
You're my friend. My gloomy, fuzzy friend.
Just hold still.

lines: *You scrub. He doesn't flinch. He watches you the whole time like you are the first sunrise he has ever agreed to look at.*
*The stain lifts. The wall is clean. And Malcolm is still here: pale, dry and blinking.*
I'm not mold anymore. I'm just a sad man in a nice coat.
Will you still want me? Without the spores?

v4_rs2.fxText: He wanted you to take charge. You did. Thoroughly.
lines: ...I'm writing a new poem. It's called 'Dry.' It's one line long. It's just your name.
*You scrub the wall. He watches with his arms crossed.*
*The stain lifts. Malcolm, dry and pale, looks at you with something very cold.*
Toxic. You'd know, wouldn't you. You've been breathing me in for weeks.
I'm leaving. I'm going to go grow somewhere that appreciates me. A cave. A basement in Portland.
*He sweeps out of the room, leaving one last poem taped to the wall. It's the word 'no' forty times.*
*You scrub. Malcolm hums something in a minor key under his breath. It's almost nice.*
*The stain lifts. He's still here. Pale. Dry. Marginally less gloomy.*
Friends. Yes. I'll allow it.
I'm still going to wear black. And write about death. But I'll do it on your couch, if that's alright.
*He holds still. You scrub until the wall is clean and quiet.*
*Malcolm straightens his coat, dry for the first time in a very long time.*
So. That happened.
We've spoken today. My quota of human contact is exhausted.
Come back next week. I'll have written something devastating about you.
You're back. Good. I've written eleven poems since breakfast. Sit. Listen. That's an order. ...Please.
*Malcolm doesn't look up from his notebook.*
I'm only here for my beret. Don't breathe on me.
Oh, it's you. My friend. I've been practicing saying that. It's getting less painful.
*A cold, dry stare.*
The wall is clean. You won. Enjoy your eggshell.
